title: Research
text:
ANRF-funded project (CRG/2023/006573)
Engineering sunflower for increased triacylglycerol (TAG) content and altered fatty acid profile using genome editing and chia genes
My current research at the University of Hyderabad focuses on engineering sunflower lipid metabolism to increase TAG accumulation and alter fatty-acid composition, including enrichment of oil with omega-3 fatty acids.
My work combines:

CRISPR/Cas9 and gRNA strategy design
Cloning and genome-editing vector construction
Sunflower transformation and tissue-culture workflows
Regeneration protocol development and optimisation
PCR-based genotyping and gene-expression analysis
GC-MS/MS method development and quantitative lipid profiling
Instrument maintenance and troubleshooting




My broader research interests centre on how lipid biosynthetic pathways are regulated and how metabolic engineering can alter storage-lipid accumulation and fatty-acid composition.
Key interests include:

TAG biosynthesis and DGAT2
Fatty-acid desaturation and FAD genes
Omega-3 fatty-acid enrichment
Lipid metabolic heterogeneity
Integrative multi-omics




I have hands-on experience in LC-MS/MS and GC-MS/MS across research and regulated bioanalytical environments. At Axis Clinicals, I worked across 34 BA/BE projects, developed 5 bioanalytical methods and validated 14 methods across 15 studies.
I am interested in extending mass-spectrometry workflows toward lipidomics, metabolomics, and molecular profiling.



My molecular biology interests include CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing, cloning, PCR, genotyping, gene-expression analysis, nucleic-acid isolation, plant transformation, and tissue culture.



I use and am developing experience with NCBI-BLAST, Primer3, CHOP-CHOP, IGV, Jalview, AutoDock Vina, GROMACS, PyMOL, Python, R, and Linux.

title: Umashankar P.
text:
Umashankar P.


Interdisciplinary Biochemist, M.Sc.



I am Umashankar P., an interdisciplinary biochemist with research experience spanning lipid metabolism, mass spectrometry, molecular biology and genome engineering.


My current research focuses on sunflower lipid metabolism through CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing and metabolic engineering. I am particularly interested in connecting molecular interventions with quantitative metabolic phenotypes using GC-MS/MS and related analytical approaches.


I am interested in PhD opportunities, research collaborations and interdisciplinary projects at the interface of plant molecular biology, lipidomics, metabolic engineering and analytical science.

title: CV
text:
Interdisciplinary Biochemist | Lipid Metabolism | Mass Spectrometry | Molecular Biology
Download CV PDF


Interdisciplinary biochemist with 4+ years of research experience spanning mass spectrometry, bioanalytical method development, molecular biology and cell-based assays. Experienced in LC-MS/MS and GC-MS/MS-based analysis, experimental design, CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing and molecular characterisation of metabolic phenotypes.



Mass spectrometry & chromatography
LC-MS/MS (Sciex 6500+); GC-MS/MS (Agilent 8890–7010D GC/TQ); HPLC/UHPLC; TLC; quantitative analysis; method development, optimisation, validation and troubleshooting.
Molecular biology & genetic engineering
CRISPR-Cas9; gRNA design; PCR; cloning; nucleic-acid isolation; gel electrophoresis; genotyping; gene-expression analysis; plant transformation and tissue culture.
Cell & microbiology
HEK293T mammalian cell culture; plant tissue culture; Gram and fungal staining.
Bioinformatics & computation
NCBI-BLAST; Primer3; CHOP-CHOP; IGV; Jalview; AutoDock Vina; GROMACS; PyMOL; Python; R; Linux.
Regulatory & quality
GLP; GCP; GDP; ICH M10; SOP drafting; laboratory documentation and instrument qualification.

title: Publications
text:
Mothe T, Umashankar P, Sultanpuram V.R. (2021).
Biosciences Biotechnology Research Asia, 18(1).
This publication arose from my M.Sc. dissertation and investigated fluoride-resistant microorganisms from contaminated groundwater and their potential for fluoride bioremediation.
Key result: Three strains tolerated up to 500 mg/L NaF; strain MB1 achieved 68% fluoride removal under the tested batch conditions.
DOI: 10.13005/bbra/2900

title: About
text:
Interdisciplinary Biochemist · Lipid Metabolism · Mass Spectrometry · Molecular Biology
I am an interdisciplinary biochemist with 4+ years of research experience spanning mass spectrometry, bioanalytical method development, molecular biology, and cell-based assays. My current work combines plant molecular biology, genome editing, metabolic engineering, and analytical chemistry to investigate sunflower lipid metabolism.
My research direction is toward integrating mass spectrometry-based lipidomics with spatial and molecular approaches to understand lipid metabolic heterogeneity in complex biological systems.
